key_insight: Large language models can learn and generalize grammar adaptation patterns from prior metamodel–grammar evolution examples, enabling automated, accurate updates to grammars after metamodel changes with less manual effort.
problem_solved: Automates the tedious and error-prone task of updating grammars to stay consistent with evolving metamodels, addressing limitations of brittle rule-based solutions when handling complex or varied grammar changes.
method: Collect pairs of old/new metamodels and corresponding grammar edits to use as adaptation examples.
Use an LLM-driven pipeline (few-shot prompting or fine-tuning) to infer and apply transformation patterns to new grammars after metamodel evolution.
Validate and refine generated grammar edits with lightweight checks (parsing/round-trip tests) and iterative feedback to improve reliability.
impact: Reduces manual engineering overhead and speeds up model-driven toolchain maintenance; enables scalable, adaptable grammar evolution workflows that integrate with existing MDE toolsets.
visual_elements: Flow diagram: Metamodel change → LLM-based adapter → Updated grammar (showing automation loop)
Before/after code diff visualization of a grammar fragment to highlight automated edits
Bar chart comparing manual effort/time or accuracy between rule-based vs LLM-based adaptation
Icon set: metamodel, grammar, LLM/brain, validation/checkmark to summarize pipeline components
paper_title: Leveraging LLMs for Grammar Adaptation: A Study on Metamodel-Grammar Co-Evolution
paper_authors: Weixing Zhang, Bowen Jiang, Rahul Sharma, Regina Hebig, Daniel Strüber
